newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER FASTEST IN FIRST LEG OF GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER FASTEST IN FIRST LEG OF GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Germany's Katja Seizinger, striving for another silver finish in the season standings, posted the fastest time in the first leg of the women's giant slalom at the World Cup Finals on Saturday.

Seizinger, who has already clinched second in the overall and in downhill and Super-G, carved her way through 48 gates on Vail Mountain in one minute, 5.81 seconds, 0.17 of a second faster than giant slalom champion Deborah Compagnoni of Italy.

Third fastest down the course, which has a vertical drop of 341 meters, was France's Sophie Lefranc in 1:06.44 followed by Austrian Anita Wachter in 1:06.51 and Spain's Ana Galindo Santolaria another .06 of a second back.
Overall champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden was sixth fastest with a first-leg time of 1:06.59, 0.78 of a second off the pace.

The 30-year-old Wachter entered the season's last giant slalom in second place behind Compagnoni with 349 points, only nine points ahead of Seizinger, winner of the first giant slalom of the season at Solden.
